title: Night Vigil Liaison Canvas and Release Notes Draft — 2026-04-15
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, night-shift focused release liaison canvas intended for the 72:00–03:00 UTC window during the April micro-deploy. It combines a tight cadence calendar, owner roster, minimal triage flow for fast decisions, and a first-pass release notes draft to be handed to customer-success in the morning.

Scope:
- Applies to the micro-deploy of platform + console services (canary -> small region rollout).
- Targets night-shift operators and on-call liaisons (not the full launch runbook).
- Not a replacement for the full cutover playbook; this is the short-form reference for the liaison on duty.

High-level goals:
- Keep surface area of changes visible during low-traffic window.
- Ensure one named liaison owns cross-team communication for each 30-minute block.
- Capture emergent issues and first-draft release notes for morning handoff.

Micro-calendar (UTC) — 2026-04-15 night window:
- 20:30 — Pre-join: verify canary pipeline green; confirm telemetry dashboards linked (owner: Priya).
- 21:00 — Preflight checklist complete, canary push scheduled (owner: Ethan).
- 21:15 — Canary deploy starts (engineers: infra-team).
- 21:30 — Liaison check-in: traffic routing and error-rate baseline (liaison: Sana).
- 22:00 — Canary telemetry review; if any SLO breach >5m, escalate (liaison: Sana).
- 22:30 — Conditional ramp to region alpha if canary stable 30m (owner: Jonah).
- 23:15 — Quick status post to #release-ops with summary snippet (liaison).
- 00:00 — Night handoff prime: compile incident notes and release notes draft (owner: Ethan).
- 01:30 — Final roll-forward decision window (product + release-engineering).
- 03:00 — Formal handover to morning crew; consolidate notes and open retros link.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any deploy):
- CI artifacts verified and SHA pinned.
- Smoke test suite (core end-to-end) passes in staging.
- Canary config matches previous canary size (no accidental scale-up).
- Telemetry dashboards: latency, error-rate (4xx/5xx), token-per-request distribution, queue depth, GPU utilization.
- Alerting: severity mappings set for this release; engineering pager rotations confirmed.
- Runbook quick links copied into the #release-ops Slack thread.
- Customer-facing comms draft ready for morning approval.

During-release quick triage flow (for night liaison):
- Signal intake: any new alert tagged REL-INC in Slack or PagerDuty.
- Triage 0–5m: confirm alert validity (false positives common at night).
- If valid: capture first-order mitigations (traffic throttle, scale-up, route bypass).
- Decision matrix:
  - Minor regressions (single-route 5xx spike <10% of requests) -> watch + mitigation, continue ramp.
  - Significant regression (error-rate >30% or latency >2x baseline for >5m) -> pause ramp, trigger team-call and rollback rubric.
  - Data-corrupting behaviors -> immediate stop + full rollback.
- Liaison responsibilities: own updates every 15 minutes while incident open, escalate to SRE lead at 2nd minute if severity rising.

Rollback rubric (short):
- Soft rollback: retract traffic splits (canary -> 0) and leave new instances running for diagnostics.
- Hard rollback: redeploy previous artifact SHA to affected AZ/region, scale to previous capacity.
- Post-rollback: mark incident as REL-INC-<date> and capture earliest log segment, relevant PRs, and probe screenshots.

Telemetry thresholds (examples to monitor live):
- 95th pct latency > 750ms (baseline 300ms) for >3 minutes -> elevated.
- 5xx rate > 1% of requests sustained 5 minutes -> investigate.
- Token generation time / GPU queue depth rising >40% over baseline -> consider burst capacity.

Communication snippets (fill-and-send templates):
- Internal Slack quick (15–30s):
  "Canary started @21:15 UTC. No elevated errors at +30m. Liaison: @Sana. Monitoring latency & 5xx. Will post next update 22:00 UTC or on change."
- Incident escalation (when triggered):
  "REL-INC: canary 21:15 -> spike 5xx 21:45 UTC. Pausing ramp. Owners: infra-team, sres. Next update +10m. Triage doc: <link>."
- Morning customer-success handoff (first-draft release note snippet):
  "Deployed: improvements to routing failover and console query latency; minor messaging fixes. No customer-facing degradation observed during canary. See full notes in morning digest."

Release notes — first-draft (morning-friendly bullets):
- Feature: improved KV-cache eviction heuristics to reduce cold-start latency on shard rebalances (platform).
- Fix: resolved intermittent 502s in console metrics endpoint under high token churn.
- Ops: updated autoscale policy for the dedicated GPU pool to reduce transient queueing during short bursts.
- Known issues: occasional tail-latency on embedded models under multi-tenant bursts; monitoring rule created (JIRA-OPS-1987).

Morning handoff checklist (what liaison must hand to morning crew):
- Single-page timeline of events (UTC), including timestamps for first anomaly, mitigations applied, and outcome.
- Links to any logs, dumps, and the PRs that went to prod.
- First-draft release notes pasted into the customer-success doc and flagged for review.
- Open action items with owners and expected delivery windows.

Post-release tagging & follow-ups:
- Tag all incident tickets with label: release-2026-04-night-vigil.
- Create retro card in Confluence within 24h with a TL;DR and a proposed action list (owner: Ethan).
- Schedule a 30m postmortem within 72h if any severity >2 incidents occurred.

Fast risk register (what to watch tonight):
- Misrouted traffic due to stale routing configs. Mitigation: verify route hashes in canary control plane preflight.
- Autoscale misfires on new binary (over-aggressive scale-down). Mitigation: keep min-instances at previous count for first 45m.
- Telemetry blips from downstream dependencies (cache/CDN). Mitigation: cross-check third-party provider status pages and fallback caches.

Open questions for morning sync (short list):
- Did the canary observe any unreported token alignment regressions? (SRE to check sampled traces.)
- Are the updated autoscale thresholds still appropriate for bursty eval workloads? (Experiment owner: infra-team.)
- Do CS/Sales need a customer-facing blurb for any subset of users?

Action items (night liaison):
- Ethan: compile timeline + paste release notes draft into CS doc by 00:15 UTC.
- Priya: verify telemetry retention snapshots saved to artifact store (by 22:15 UTC).
- Sana: monitor 5xx/latency dashboards and post 22:00 update to #release-ops.
- Jonah: stand ready to initiate regional ramp if canary stable at 22:30.

Appendix — quick links (useful during vigil):
- Staging smoke run results: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/3581
- Production telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/release-night
- Handoff doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RELEASE-VIGIL-2026-04

Notes & provenance:
- This document is intentionally compact: pick up the full cutover playbook if you need step-by-step rollback scripts or runbook automation.
- Keep this doc alive during the shift (edit in-place) and ensure the morning handoff summarizes changes made while on duty.

End of canvas.
